hook_text: By 1914, a map of Africa looked like a quilt in seven colours. Only two pieces kept their own.
clip_script: Britain: Egypt to the Cape, and Nigeria in the west. France: the Sahara and West Africa. Germany: Namibia, Tanzania, Cameroon, Togo. Belgium: the Congo. Portugal: Angola and Mozambique. Italy: Libya and the Horn. Spain: a few small pieces. Only Ethiopia and Liberia stayed free. Why? Factories needed rubber, palm oil, cotton and copper, and markets to sell to. Nations wanted prestige and feared their rivals. Britain guarded the Suez Canal. Racist ideas called conquest a civilising mission. And new machines, steamships, quinine and the Maxim gun, made it possible. Money, power, false beliefs and machines.
visual_style: A whiteboard map of Africa filling in with seven hatched patterns and two blank areas, then four labelled boxes for the causes and a row of technology icons.
pacing: Fast map tour, then a clear count of causes.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to weigh which cause mattered most.
